subject: Clarify: microburst credits, small-batch rounding, and long-context charge floor
messages:
From: Ethan Edmonds <ethan.edmonds@clearmap.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@clearmap.ai
Date: 2028-05-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on small-batch rounding + microburst credits

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked great. Procurement had a few follow-ups on how billing will behave for our use case: short, frequent inference calls (avg 120 tokens roundtrip) with occasional long-context requests (30k–60k tokens).

Two specific asks:
- How are very small calls accounted for against the minimum charge window? Do you round per-call up to the min quantum, or do you aggregate across a short time window?
- We expect microbursts (hundreds of tiny calls) — do you provide crediting from reserved capacity (e.g., burst credits) or do those just count towards overage at the per-token rate?

We also need an example invoice line that shows how a 30k token context call and 3,000 small calls in a day would be billed so our finance team can model spend.

Appreciate a short write-up so we can finalize the MAA redlines.

Best,
Ethan
Procurement Lead, Clearmap.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Edmonds <ethan.edmonds@clearmap.ai>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-09T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on small-batch rounding + microburst credits

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks. Summary first, then a worked example attached.

Short answers up front:
- Small-call aggregation: We bill tokens consumed, but there is a configurable invoicing quantum (default 50-token rounding). By default we aggregate within a 60s rolling window per API key to avoid charging each tiny call up to the quantum. That means 3,000 ~120-token calls in a day would be aggregated into windows; you typically hit fewer quanta than calls.
- Microburst credits: For Dedicated and some committed tiers we provide a burst credit pool that offsets overage when short bursts exceed reserved throughput. Credits are applied before overage charges and are consumed based on effective token-weighted units.
- Long-context calls: Context length itself is charged at tokens consumed. For contexts >32k we normalize by model variant (we have slabed pricing beyond 32k for memory pressure) and apply a long-context surcharge if the call forces fallback to a high-memory instance.

I've attached a worked example with three lines: (1) reserve consumption, (2) microburst credit application, (3) invoice reconciliation showing rounding and remaining overage.

Action for procurement: if you want the 60s window tightened to 10s (less aggregation) there is a configuration and we can turn it on per-customer, but it will change expected unit economics.

-Karthik
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Ethan Edmonds <ethan.edmonds@clearmap.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-05-10T15:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on small-batch rounding + microburst credits

Ethan — adding some clarity and a proposal we can include in the MAA.

Proposal (concise):
- Aggregation window: 60s rolling (default). For Clearmap pilot we’ll keep 60s but allow a 14-day trial of 10s aggregation to validate economics.
- Minimum quantum: 50-token quantum for rounding. Relevant only when a single aggregation window totals <50 tokens (rare with 120-token avg).
- Microburst credits: For the pilot we propose 50k token-equivalent burst credits per billing month. Credits are consumed in the following priority: reserved capacity -> burst credits -> overage. Any unused credits do not roll.
- Long-context surcharge: Calls >32k will be billed at model token rate + 25% context surcharge if they use the high-memory serving variant; we can add a cap (e.g., max surcharge applied once per heavy call).

Invoice example (high level):
1) Reserved committed units: 1,000,000 tokens (monthly commit)
2) Microburst credits applied: 50,000 tokens
3) Usage: 1,120,000 tokens total (includes 30k long-context call)
4) Billable usage after credits: 70,000 tokens -> rounded using 50-token quantum => 70,000 stays 70,000 (no additional rounding impact)
5) Surcharge: 30,000 * 25% = 7,500 token-equivalent surcharge -> billed at token rate

We should put a line in the MAA appendix that describes credit expiration and the allocation priority. Karthik — legal wants a short phrase that caps the surcharge "per-call" to avoid open-ended fees.

-Vanessa
Director, Enterprise Sales Ops

1) Can you send the MAA redline with the recommended appendix language for burst credits and the per-call surcharge cap? We prefer the cap be expressed as "no more than 1.5x the standard per-token price for any single call that triggers the high-memory variant."
2) Please confirm whether the 14-day trial of 10s aggregation requires any infra changes on our side (we want it zero-footprint).

If both answers are yes/no as appropriate, procurement will sign the MAA and route the DocuSign to me (procurement asked me to confirm the docusign link earlier).

Best,
Ethan
